red — Admissions relevant but not conclusive — Claimant’s conditional answer to hypothetical sequence not admission of actual signal colour — Evidence Act 1950, ss 17, 18, 21 and 31 EVIDENCE — judgments.catchwords: CONTRACT — Formation — Design and build contract — Manuscript handover date inserted into acceptance — Counter-proposal introducing materially different completion term — Contract concluded by performance despite continuing disagreement on time — Neither employer’s date nor contractor’s proposed period accepted — Obligation to complete within reasonable time — Delay established but not extinguishing accrued entitlement to payment for work done — Contracts Act 1950, ss 7(a) and 74(1). CONSTRUCTION LAW — Contract terms — Incorporation of standard conditions — Borang JKR 203 contemplated in correspondence — Prospective references and use of certificate formats insufficient to establish incorporation — Standard form and applicable clauses not produced — Administrative practice distinguished from contractual incorporation — Rights governed by agreed terms and general law. CONSTRUCTION LAW — Payment — Certificates issued by contractor’s own consultants — No contractual provision making certification final and binding — Certificates cogent but not conclusive evidence — Employer’s valuation in statutory payment response constituting admission — Unexplained departure from admitted valuation rejected — Rectifiable defects addressed through counterclaim without double deduction — Evidence Act 1950, ss 17 and 21. CONSTRUCTION LAW — Variations — Proof of employer’s authorisation — Site supervisor’s authority expressly confined to verification and monitoring — Wider ostensible authority not established — Burden remaining on contractor to prove instructions — Variations admitted in employer’s payment response allowed — Balance unsupported by instructions or approvals disallowed — Alternative quantum meruit claim unpleaded and unsupported by independent evidence of reasonable value — Contracts Act 1950, s 71 — Evidence Act 1950, ss 101, 103 and 114(g). CONSTRUCTION LAW — Termination — Persistent non-payment of progress claims — Cessation of works at employer’s instance — Contractor’s refusal to resume while unpaid not repudiatory on facts — Employer’s subsequent termination unjustified — Prevention principle — Accrued payment rights preserved — Retention recoverable subject to set-off for proved defects — Contracts Act 1950, s 54. DAMAGES — Building contract — Delay, completion and rectification costs — Delay established but attributable loss not quantified — Nominal damages awarded — Gross completion expenditure not recoverable following employer’s wrongful prevention and termination — Excess over unpaid original contract price not proved — Separately established rectification costs and materials supplied allowed — Unsubstantiated claims for missing items, salvaged steel and storage charges dismissed — Contracts Act 1950, s 74(1). TORT — Negligence — Architect engaged by design and build contractor — Alleged over-certification — Duty of care to employer left undecided — Employer neither relied nor paid on impugned certificate — No causative loss or departure from professional standard proved — Authorisation of variations distinguished from architectural measurement — Claim against architect dismissed. CONSTRUCTION LAW — Adjudication — Final determination by court — Adjudication decision temporarily binding — Trial judgment determining parties’ substantive rights — Contractor’s recovery subject to counterclaim set-off — Payments under adjudication decision or enforcement order to be brought into account — Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012, s 13.

judgments.catchwords: CIVIL PROCEDURE — Service out of jurisdiction — Civil Procedure Convention — Meaning of convention which “subsists” between Malaysia and foreign country — British-German Legal Assistance Convention 1928 extended and continued in force for Malaysia — Incorporation into Malaysian domestic law unnecessary — Convention’s existence as international arrangement a fact triggering domestic procedural options — Service through German judicial authorities available in principle — Rules of Court 2012, O 11 r 6(1). CIVIL PROCEDURE — Service out of jurisdiction — Compliance with law of country of service — Formal substituted service in Germany — German translations not certified by diplomatic or consular officer or official or sworn translator — Embassy listing and professional association membership insufficient — Treaty certification requirement protecting conditions of inter-State judicial assistance — Actual receipt and absence of demonstrated prejudice not establishing valid service — Service on both defendants set aside — Rules of Court 2012, O 11 rr 5(2) and 5(3) — British-German Legal Assistance Convention 1928, art 3(e). EVIDENCE — Foreign law — Conflicting expert opinions — Final decision of superior German court declaring service on first defendant unlawful — Plaintiff not party to foreign proceedings — No binding estoppel — Foreign decision carrying substantial evidential weight on legality of acts of its own judicial administration — Independent assessment of evidence — Common translation defect also invalidating service on second defendant — Evidence Act 1950, ss 45(1), 51, 101 and 103. CIVIL PROCEDURE — Irregularity — Defective service abroad — Breach of foreign law and treaty requirements — Actual receipt not curing defect — Comity and foreign sovereignty — General curative powers unavailable — Dispensation with service not available to validate retrospectively acts contrary to foreign law — Rules of Court 2012, O 1A, O 2 r 1, O 11 rr 5(2) and 5(3), and O 62 r 14. CIVIL PROCEDURE — Jurisdiction — Submission — Appearance entered followed by timely jurisdictional challenge — References to merits in affidavits explaining forum objections — No defence filed or substantive relief sought — Appointment of Malaysian solicitors not authority to accept service — Conduct consistent with maintaining jurisdictional challenge — No submission or waiver — Rules of Court 2012, O 12 rr 9 and 10. CONFLICT OF LAWS — Jurisdiction and forum — Liquidators’ claims against foreign shareholder and director — Alleged unlawful dividends, fraudulent trading, conspiracy and transfer of Malaysian land — Malaysian statutory claims, assets, witnesses and co-defendants — Risk of duplicated proceedings and inconsistent findings — Availability of German courts and uncertainty of enforcement considered — Malaysia clearly most appropriate forum — Invalid service distinct from jurisdiction and propriety of leave to serve out — Service order and requests for service maintained — Courts of Judicature Act 1964, s 23 — Companies Act 2016, ss 131, 133 and 540 — Rules of Court 2012, O 11 r 1. CIVIL PROCEDURE — Costs — Applications succeeding on principal relief but failing on alternative jurisdiction and forum grounds — Service set aside — Defendants entitled to costs with reduction reflecting issues on which plaintiff prevailed — Rules of Court 2012, O 59 r 3(2).

judgments.catchwords: Mahkamah mendapati tempat barang kes dijumpai merupakan stor tempat penyimpanan barang-barang dan kedua-dua pertuduhan pindaan berkisar di rumah beralamat di DKDT 142I, Jalan Sir Ibrahim, 11600 Jelutong, di dalam Daerah Timur Laut, di dalam Negeri Pulau Pinang. Apa yang dibuktikan hanyalah kaitan umum OKT dengan rumah, kewujudan anak-anak kunci, penemuan pasport dan dakwaan bahawa beliau mengetahui lokasi bilik. Keadaan-keadaan tersebut tidak mencukupi untuk membuktikan bahawa OKT mempunyai milikan eksklusif atau milikan bersama terhadap dadah. Oleh itu, elemen kedua gagal dibuktikan. Di peringkat akhir kes pendakwaan, Mahkamah setelah membuat penilaian maksimum ke atas segala keterangan yang dikemukakan oleh saksi-saksi pendakwaan berserta eksibit-eksibit yang dikemukakan di hadapan Mahkamah ini dan setelah mempertimbangkan hujahan kedua-dua pihak di peringkat ini, Mahkamah dengan ini berpuas hati dan mendapati bahawa pihak pendakwaan, di akhir kes pendakwaan, telah gagal membuktikan kes prima facie ke atas OKT sebagaimana yang dituduhkan, sepertimana yang diperuntukkan di bawah Seksyen 180(1) KTJ. Mahkamah dengan ini memerintahkan OKT untuk dilepas dan dibebaskan daripada pertuduhan ini.

judgments.title: Santhi A/P Ganga v JANAGI A/P J VALU
judgments.catchwords: Originating Summons - to terminate the co-ownership of the subject immovable property, direct its sale, and divide the net proceeds between the Applicant and the Respondent. Termination of co-ownership - registration of title under the NLC confers merely prima facie legal title and does not automatically vest absolute beneficial ownership in equity - as one hundred percent (100%) of the beneficial ownership resided exclusively with the Deceased during his lifetime and has now devolved onto his estate, there is absolutely no legal or factual basis for the Applicant to seek the termination of the co-proprietorship or the sale of the Property under s. 145(1) & (2)(c) of the NLC Registration of non-Muslim marriages - de facto cohabitation, regardless of longevity, does not translate into a lawful marriage, nor does it generate statutory rights over matrimonial assets. Indefeasibility of title – having been obtained through misrepresentation, the Applicant’s registered interest is rendered legally infirm, and she is barred from invoking the doctrine of indefeasibility Equitable relief - he who comes to equity must come with clean hands - such powers are not exercised arbitrarily, but require a threshold of credible and sufficient material to warrant judicial intervention
